# Visualization with RUBELLA

Plotting a single brain map:
```py
from rubella import plotting
help(plotting.plot_brain)
```

Example:
```py
template_file = '/path_to_template_folder/commonspace_template.nii.gz'
brain_mask_file = data_obj.brain_mask_file

# GC_dict was generated by computing global connectivity
data = GC_dict[data_obj.img_id_list[0]] # taking the first image 


fig,ax_list,cbar_list = plotting.plot_brain(
        data,brain_mask_file,template_file,
        fig=None,ax=None,plot_size_scale=0.1,
        plane='coronal', selected_slices='all', slices_per_row=6, # slice selection
        cmap='cold_hot', vmax=0.1, vmin=None, plot_cbar=True, # cmap range
        fixed_threshold=0.02,percent_thresholding=False,top_percent=10, # image thresholding
        )
```

Plotting multiple brain maps:
```py
from rubella import plotting
template_file = '/path_to_template_folder/commonspace_template.nii.gz'
brain_mask_file = data_obj.brain_mask_file

# generate a list of maps to plot in a single figure
data_list = [GC_dict[img_id] for img_id in data_obj.img_id_list]

fig,ax_list,cbar_list = plotting.plot_many_brains(
        data_list,brain_mask_file,template_file,
        fig=None,ax_list=None,plot_size_scale=0.1,num_brain_per_row=1,
        plane='coronal', selected_slices='all', slices_per_row=6, # slice selection
        cmap='cold_hot', vmax=0.1, vmin=None, plot_cbar=True, # cmap range
        fixed_threshold=0.02,percent_thresholding=False,top_percent=10, # image thresholding
        )
```
